newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO, NOVOTNA UPSET AT HILTON HEAD ISLAND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO, NOVOTNA UPSET AT HILTON HEAD ISLAND.

text.p: Second seed and defending champion Arantxa Sanchez Vicario was hoping the start to the clay court season at the Family Circle Cup would give her a new lease on life.

Instead the Spaniard was left looking for answers to the first extended title drought of her career after being trounced in the third set by 13th-seeded South African Amanda Coetzer in a 6-2 5-7 6-0 defeat.
"I'm in a very tough (stretch)," said Sanchez just one day after being encouraged by her victory in her first match this year on clay.
Sanchez has a terribly disappointing 8-7 match record this year and has not won a tournament since last May despite reaching numerous finals.
"I think any athlete goes through that, some ups and downs in their life, and it's happening to me for the first time in 12 years as a professional. But I just have to keep going," Sanchez said.
The tournament also lost its third seed, Czech veteran Jana Novotna, a semifinalist here last year who fell victim to the booming serve of 14th-seeded Dutchwoman Brenda Schultz-McCarthy 6-3 6-3.
While other top players struggled, new world number one Martina Hingis just kept rolling merrily along.
The 16-year-old Swiss phenom raised her 1997 match record to an unblemished 28-0 with a 6-3 6-3 third-round victory over 36th-ranked Austrian Barbara Schett.

"I was hitting a big forehand today, which is not very usual for me, but I was playing very well and at a good standard for my game," said the supremely confident teenager in the hunt for her sixth title of the year.
The biggest challenge for Hingis may be to avoid injury in her quarter-final match with Wiltrud Probst of Germany.
Probst reached the quarters after both her second and third round opponents were forced to retire with wrist injuries, the latest eighth seed Irina Spirlea of Romania.
"Mine is doing fine," Hingis said of her wrists.

Also advancing was fifth-seeded two-time champion Conchita Martinez of Spain, who stopped Jennifer Capriati 6-0 5-7 6-4, and seventh-seeded German Anke Huber, who saved five match points before beating ninth seed Iva Majoli of Croatia 3-6 7-6 (7-5) 6-3.
Sanchez never managed anything like Huber's comeback, despite her reputation as a fighter.
The Spaniard commited an unthinkable 68 unforced errors and seemed to have no response for Coetzer's stead array of pinpoint shots that helped beat Sanchez into submission in the deciding set.
"The third set I tried to go for a lot of shots, and that was a mistake," Sanchez said. "She was more patient than me today and that's why she beat me."
